title: Chemical Reactions in Everyday Lives

competencies.text: Explain common reaction types: decomposition, acid on carbonates, acids on metals, combustion.
Identify reaction types in daily activities: baking, cleaning, burning.

days.title: What Is a Chemical Reaction?
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

This week you will explain four common reaction types — decomposition, acid on carbonates, acids on metals and combustion — and identify them in daily activities like baking, cleaning and cooking.

🔬 Reactants and Products

A chemical reaction changes one or more substances (reactants) into new substances (products) with different properties. Atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed, so the total mass stays the same.

Reactants → Products

🧪 Signs That a Reaction Happened

SignEveryday example
Gas bubbles (not from boiling)Antacid tablet fizzing in water
Color changeIron gate turning reddish-brown (rust)
Heat or light given offLPG flame on a stove
A solid (precipitate) forms in a liquidSoap scum in hard water
New smellMilk turning sour

⚖️ Physical vs Chemical Change

Melting ice, dissolving sugar and cutting paper are physical changes — the substance stays the same. Burning paper, cooking an egg and rusting are chemical changes — a new substance forms and the change is hard to reverse. One sign alone is not proof: boiling water also makes bubbles, but it is still water.

✅ Quick Check

3 questions — read each explanation.

scenario.text: Which of these is a CHEMICAL change?

choices.label: Paper burning to ash and smoke
Ice melting into liquid water in a glass
Sugar dissolving in a glass of hot coffee
A sheet of paper being cut into small pieces

scenario.explanation: Burning makes new substances (ash, carbon dioxide, water vapor). The others change form or size but the substance stays the same.

scenario.text: Water boils and forms bubbles in a kettle. Why is this NOT a chemical reaction?

choices.label: The bubbles are still water, just as a gas
The bubbles form only because of the heat source
No color change happened inside the kettle
Kettles are made of metal, so nothing can react

scenario.explanation: Boiling changes water from liquid to gas — a physical change. No new substance forms, even though bubbles appear.

scenario.text: In the reaction "wood + oxygen → ash + carbon dioxide + water," which are the REACTANTS?

choices.label: Wood and oxygen
Ash and carbon dioxide
Carbon dioxide and water
Ash, carbon dioxide and water

scenario.explanation: Reactants are written on the left of the arrow; they are used up. Products are on the right; they are formed.

days.title: Four Reaction Types
days.content:
⚗️ The Four Types

TypeGeneral patternEveryday example
DecompositionOne compound → two or more simpler substances2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂ (peroxide fizzing on a wound)
Acid + carbonateacid + carbonate → salt + water + CO₂Vinegar + baking soda fizzing
Acid + metalacid + metal → salt + hydrogen gasMuriatic acid bubbling on zinc or iron
Combustionfuel + oxygen → CO₂ + H₂O + heat and lightLPG stove, candle, jeepney engine

🔎 How to Tell Them Apart

  • One reactant only? It is decomposition — often needs heat, light or a catalyst (an enzyme in blood speeds up peroxide breakdown).
  • Acid fizzing? Check what it touched. With a carbonate (baking soda, limestone, eggshell) the gas is CO₂, which puts out a flame. With a metal the gas is hydrogen, which pops with a flame.
  • Fuel + oxygen with heat and light? It is combustion. If oxygen is limited, incomplete combustion makes soot and deadly carbon monoxide.

🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each reaction or term to its description. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

match.right: One compound breaks into simpler substances
match.why: Example: hydrogen peroxide breaking into water and oxygen.

match.right: Makes a salt, water and carbon dioxide
match.why: Vinegar and baking soda fizz because CO₂ is released.

match.right: Makes a salt and hydrogen gas
match.why: Hydrogen gas makes a squeaky pop when lit.

match.right: Fuel reacts with oxygen, giving heat and light
match.why: Burning LPG, wood and diesel are combustion.

match.right: Too little oxygen; forms soot and CO
match.why: A yellow, smoky flame signals incomplete burning.

match.right: Makes a squeaky pop with a flame
Speeds up a reaction without being used up
match.why: An enzyme in blood speeds up peroxide decomposition.

days.title: Reactions at Home
days.content:
🍰 In the Kitchen

  • Baking: baking powder contains sodium bicarbonate and a dry acid. When wet and heated, they react (acid + carbonate) and release CO₂, which makes puto and cake rise.
  • Cooking with LPG: butane and propane burn in oxygen (combustion). A blue flame means complete combustion; a yellow, sooty flame means not enough air.

🧽 Cleaning

  • Descaling a kettle: white scale is calcium carbonate. Vinegar (acetic acid) dissolves it with fizzing (acid + carbonate).
  • Muriatic acid on tiles: it removes stains but also attacks metal fixtures, releasing hydrogen (acid + metal). Use with gloves and ventilation.

🩹 First Aid and the Body

Hydrogen peroxide fizzes on a wound because an enzyme in blood (catalase) speeds up its decomposition into water and oxygen. Antacids neutralize excess stomach acid; some contain carbonates and release CO₂, which is why you may burp.

🔩 Rusting

Iron slowly reacts with oxygen and water to form rust (iron oxide). Salt water speeds it up, which is why coastal roofs and gates rust faster. Paint, oil and galvanizing (zinc coating) keep oxygen and water away.

🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Identify and reason about reactions in daily life. Read every explanation. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

scenario.text: Your LPG stove suddenly burns with a yellow, sooty flame instead of a blue one. What does this MOST likely mean?

choices.label: Not enough oxygen is mixing with the gas
The LPG tank is completely full of fuel
The flame is hotter than normal and is safer
The stove is changing LPG into hydrogen gas

scenario.explanation: A yellow, smoky flame shows incomplete combustion from too little air. It wastes fuel and can produce carbon monoxide, so the burner should be cleaned or adjusted.

scenario.text: White scale builds up inside a kettle. Soaking it in vinegar makes it fizz and disappear. What reaction is this?

choices.label: Acid reacting with a carbonate
Decomposition of the water itself
Combustion of the white scale layer
Acid reacting with the metal kettle body

scenario.explanation: The scale is calcium carbonate. Acetic acid reacts with it to make a soluble salt, water and CO₂ — the fizz.

scenario.text: A student drops a zinc strip into dilute hydrochloric acid. Bubbles form, and a lit splint held at the tube makes a squeaky pop. Which gas formed?

choices.label: Hydrogen
Carbon dioxide
Oxygen
Water vapor

scenario.explanation: Acid + metal produces a salt and hydrogen gas. Hydrogen burns with a squeaky pop; CO₂ would put the flame out.

scenario.text: Iron gates in a coastal barangay rust much faster than those in an inland town. What is the BEST explanation?

choices.label: Salty, moist air speeds up rusting
Sea breezes are colder, causing rust
Sunlight on the coast melts the paint
Inland air has no oxygen to react with

scenario.explanation: Rusting needs oxygen and water; dissolved salt helps the reaction go faster. Coastal air is humid and salty.

scenario.text: Which household plan would BEST slow the rusting of a new steel gate?

choices.label: Paint it to keep out air and moisture
Wash it with salt water once a week
Keep it wet so dust cannot stick to it
Leave it bare so the metal can breathe

scenario.explanation: Paint forms a barrier between the iron and the oxygen and water it needs to rust. Salt and moisture would speed rusting up.

days.title: Combustion and Chemical Safety
days.content:
🔥 Complete vs Incomplete Combustion

CompleteIncomplete
Oxygen supplyPlentyLimited
FlameBlue, cleanYellow-orange, sooty
ProductsCO₂ + H₂O + much heatCO, soot (C), less heat

☠️ Carbon Monoxide (CO)

CO has no color and no smell. It binds to hemoglobin in blood more strongly than oxygen, so the body is starved of oxygen. Never run a generator, charcoal stove or car engine inside a closed room or garage.

⚠️ Reactions to Avoid

  • Bleach + ammonia → toxic chloramine gas; bleach + acid (muriatic, vinegar) → chlorine gas.
  • Muriatic acid is corrosive — use gloves, eye protection and good ventilation.
  • LPG leaks: no switches or flames; open doors and windows; close the regulator.

🧠 Why This Matters

Knowing the reaction type helps you predict the products — and the dangers. Combustion can produce CO; acids on metals produce flammable hydrogen; mixing cleaners can release toxic gases.

🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Lab

3 lives, 6 keys. You need 70% (5 of 6). Read each explanation.

escape.text: What are the main products of COMPLETE combustion of LPG?

choices.label: Carbon dioxide and water
Carbon monoxide and soot
Hydrogen and oxygen gas
Salt and hydrogen gas

escape.explanation: With enough oxygen, hydrocarbon fuels burn completely to CO₂ and H₂O, releasing heat and light.

escape.text: Hydrogen peroxide breaking into water and oxygen is which reaction type?

choices.label: Decomposition
Combustion
Acid + metal
Acid + carbonate

escape.explanation: One compound breaks into simpler substances — that is decomposition.

escape.text: Why is carbon monoxide especially dangerous?

choices.label: It is odorless and blocks oxygen in the blood
It smells strongly and makes the eyes water a lot
It makes the room much colder very quickly
It turns into liquid that floods the lungs

escape.explanation: CO cannot be seen or smelled, and it binds to hemoglobin, preventing the blood from carrying oxygen.

escape.text: Which gas is produced when vinegar reacts with baking soda?

choices.label: Carbon dioxide
Hydrogen
Oxygen
Chlorine gas (Cl₂)

escape.explanation: Acid + carbonate → salt + water + CO₂. That gas makes the fizz.

escape.text: A family runs a generator inside a closed garage during a brownout. What is the BEST advice?

choices.label: Move it outdoors, away from doors and windows
Keep the garage closed so the fumes stay out of the house
Run it only at night when the air is cooler
Put a fan beside it inside the garage to cool it

escape.explanation: Generators produce carbon monoxide. It must run outdoors where the gas can disperse, far from openings into the house.

escape.text: Which observation BEST shows that a chemical reaction happened?

choices.label: A new gas forms when two liquids are mixed
Ice cubes melt into water on a warm wooden table
Salt disappears when stirred into water
A rubber band stretches and snaps back

escape.explanation: A new substance (gas) forming from mixed liquids signals a chemical change. The others are physical changes.
